title: Suspected stroke at a first aid post
setting: First aid post. Patient walked in stumbling, complaining of sudden severe vertigo, double vision, and being unable to coordinate their movements.
verdictExplanation: Sudden onset of severe vertigo, ataxia (unsteady gait), and double vision indicate a suspected posterior circulation stroke. Even if the standard FAST test is negative, these neurological red flags mean they are sick: requires immediate 999 escalation.

er.pupilSize: Equal and reactive, but double vision reported

er.disability: Severe ataxia (unsteady gait), double vision, disoriented

history.history: Began feeling suddenly dizzy and completely off-balance 20 minutes ago while walking in the park
history.additional: Struggling to walk straight, feels like the room is spinning violently

followUp.question: The FAST test is negative, but the patient has sudden severe vertigo and ataxia. What is the correct priority management?

options.text: Call 999 immediately for a suspected stroke, noting the exact time of onset and keeping the patient calm
Tell them they are just dizzy from low blood sugar and give them a sugary drink
Lie them flat on their back and encourage them to sleep off the vertigo
Encourage them to walk around the post to regain their balance

followUp.explanation: Not all strokes present with FAST symptoms. Sudden onset of severe vertigo, ataxia (loss of balance), and visual disturbances suggest a posterior circulation stroke. This requires an immediate 999 call and exact time of onset, just like a FAST-positive stroke.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Suspect stroke despite negative FAST due to sudden ataxia/vertigo. Call 999 immediately, keep calm, protect airway.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected acute stroke. Monitor airway. Check BGL to rule out hypoglycaemia. Administer oxygen if SpO₂ <94%. Prepare for rapid transport.
